entities.summary:
Herintsalama Andriamiasy Rajaonarivelo emerged as a pivotal figure in Madagascar's early 21st-century political landscape, serving as the nation's Prime Minister from October 2025 to March 2026. Prior to his brief but impactful premiership, Rajaonarivelo was a prominent economist and businessman, most notably as Chairman of the Board of Directors of BNI Madagascar, one of the country's leading financial institutions. His appointment to the highest executive office, following a period of economic uncertainty and political flux, underscored a prevailing national desire for technocratic leadership and stability in the Indian Ocean island nation.

Rajaonarivelo's tenure as Prime Minister, though spanning only six months, was characterized by an emphasis on economic stabilization, foreign investment attraction, and public sector reform. Leveraging his extensive background in finance, he initiated discussions on debt restructuring and prioritized measures aimed at improving the business climate to attract much-needed capital for infrastructure and development projects. His administration also focused on streamlining government operations and combating corruption, challenges that had long plagued Malagasy governance. These efforts, while nascent, signaled a clear direction towards market-oriented policies and greater fiscal discipline.
